decision: Measured the starting point with drama bench: backbone 128 rows 583 ms (moe 331, linear 193, full 34), tower 128 rows 166 ms, decode 17.3 ms backbone plus 6.7 ms tower GPU; the README's 1.1 s and 25 ms were taken under load

decision: Scored the current engine against the float32 oracle before touching anything: rel L2 hidden 6.5e-7, cand 3.3e-7, tower 5.0e-7, top-1 1.0

decision: Dense prefill gets a simdgroup-matrix GEMM (64x64 tile, K step 32, bf16 widened to fp32 in threadgroup memory, fp32 accumulate) used when M > 1; the GEMV stays for M = 1
why: the GEMV re-reads every activation row once per output row, so at 128 rows it runs at about 2 TFLOPS; per-row results stay independent of the chunk so the prefix cache test still matches bit for bit

decision: Sampling moves to the GPU in double-float arithmetic (pairs of fp32) so picks match the CPU sampler's double precision except with probability about 1e-14 per decision; one command buffer per frame, pipelined one frame ahead when not tracing
why: fp32 sampling would flip a top-p or argmax decision about once per 1e6 samples, which would change the e2e seeds; the CPU round trips cost about 6 ms of a 31 ms frame
evidence: delegated to a worktree agent, brief in the transcript

decision: First GEMM (64x64 tile, K step 32) was slower than the GEMV: 855 ms against 583 at 128 rows, and 395 ms against 42 at 8 rows
why: 18 KB of threadgroup memory left one threadgroup per core, and at small M only N/64 threadgroups exist; measured, not guessed
result: reverted to a templated kernel so tiles could be measured

decision: Built drama kbench, a synthetic-data micro-benchmark of the GEMV against eight tile shapes, and chose tiles by M and N from it: GEMV up to 4 rows (16 for N up to 512), 16x32x16 for small M, 32x32x16 from 96 rows, 64x32x16 at 128 rows for N of 8192 and up
why: 32x32x16 reaches 8.4 TFLOPS at M=128 N=8192 against 1.5 for the GEMV; narrow N has too few threadgroups for a GEMM to win below 16 rows; five repeats of the 8192x2048 shape agree within 2 percent
result: 128-row backbone 583 to 507 ms, tower 166 to 39 ms, non-expert backbone work now 87 ms; faithfulness table unchanged (hidden 6.0e-7)

decision: Added finer bench stages (experts, shared, gdn, attn); the deltas for stages before the router are confounded because skipping them changes the routing and thus the expert work
why: only the no-moe and no-experts deltas are trustworthy for sizing; the rest need a per-kernel harness
result: experts about 410 ms of 507 at 128 rows

decision: Tiled FP8 expert kernels for prefill: one threadgroup per (expert, 32 output columns), rows in simdgroup-matrix blocks of 8 up to 32 per pass, weight tile dequantized once per pass; chosen when rows > 1
why: the row kernels dequantized every weight once per routed token and re-read the activations once per output row; parity against them 1.2e-6 on synthetic experts
result: 128-row backbone 507 to 230 ms (experts about 410 to 108 ms); faithfulness table unchanged (hidden 5.8e-7, top-1 1.0)

decision: Dropped the per-M tile table for one tile (32x32x16) at every M above 1; GEMV only at M = 1
why: the chunk-independence test caught it: different tiles sum in different orders, and the prefix cache test needs a row's result to be the same in any chunk of 2 or more rows
result: tests green; costs about 8 ms of the 128-row prefill against the best mixed table

decision: Built drama profile: times each kernel group alone on the buffers a real forward left behind and scales by layer count; at 128 rows the experts are 84 ms (close to the bandwidth floor for 30 GB of FP8 weights), the GDN recurrence 24 ms, dense GEMMs about 40 ms, narrow projections (N 1 and 32) 9 ms
why: the stage-skip deltas were confounded by routing; this harness is the measurement the remaining work is planned from

decision: GEMV now spreads 32-token tiles over the grid and stays the kernel for outputs of 64 columns or fewer at any M; prefill chunk raised from 128 to 512 rows
why: a GEMM with one column tile walks K alone (the N=1 shared-expert gate cost 3.6 ms per forward); every chunk re-reads all 30 GB of expert weights, so a 300-row clip in three chunks paid that three times; both changes keep every row's result bit-identical

decision: GDN recurrence split: each head's 128x128 state is now owned by 512 threads (4 per column) with the two per-token dot products combined from 4 partial sums in a fixed order; 4 chosen over 1, 2 and 8
why: one threadgroup of 128 threads per head left the GPU almost idle and the 128-float state per thread spilled; 300-row cost 51 to 18 ms, decode 0.40 to 0.24 ms, outputs and state within 2e-7 of the single-column kernel

decision: One chunk of 300 rows now prefills in 443 ms (360 backbone, 83 tower) against about 1.8 s in three 128-row chunks before; 128 rows 191 ms against 583
why: the task's target was well under a second for a 10 s reference clip

decision: Decode MoE kernels left alone: at one row the row kernels read the 8 active experts at about 360 GB/s (1.6 ms gate-up, 1.1 ms down per 40 layers), which is the memory floor; the 2048-threadgroup down launch costs 27 us per layer
why: the task asked to look at the down kernel's launch shape; measured, it is not the limiter
